atoms.statement: Adopt the proven three-phase adversarial architecture (FIND → VERIFY → SYNTHESIZE) and replace the broken deep-LLM component (deep:deep_failed) with this new multi-agent orchestrator.
atoms.test: Verify that the old `deep:deep_failed` path is removed/disabled and the new system follows a distinct FIND, VERIFY, SYNTHESIZE execution flow.

atoms.statement: Separate the audit into two distinct modes: the existing nightly static guard and a new milestone-triggered adversarial deep audit, which is invoked on-demand.
atoms.test: Confirm that the nightly static audit runs independently and the adversarial deep audit can only be triggered manually or via specific milestone hooks, never by the nightly cron.

atoms.statement: Enforce a hard floor of at least 20 concurrent active agents during FIND and VERIFY phases, maintaining this floor via a refill-queue worker pool that replaces the current maxParallelAgents cap.
atoms.test: Run a stress test with >20 jobs and verify that the system consistently maintains 20+ active agent processes, not just queued, as measured by live PID sampling.

atoms.statement: Prove real parallelism (not sequential) by sampling live audit-agent PIDs, recording peak_concurrency and a concurrency timeline in the audit report, asserting peak >= 20 when sufficient work exists.
atoms.test: Generate an audit report that includes a concurrency timeline and peak_concurrency metric, demonstrating that >= 20 agents were active simultaneously during a test run with sufficient work.

atoms.statement: Use ONLY Claude CLI and Codex CLI for all audit agents, balancing provider/model/reasoning profiles between finder/verifier slots.
atoms.test: Verify that no raw API calls or other LLM providers (e.g., Gemini) are used, and that agent invocation exclusively uses Claude CLI and Codex CLI.

atoms.statement: Implement provider-aware rate-limit handling with backoff/retry for 429/usage limits, balancing agent distribution (e.g., ~50/50) and re-distributing jobs across Claude and Codex providers to maintain the concurrency floor.
atoms.test: Simulate 429 errors from one provider and verify that the system retries with backoff, rebalances jobs to the other provider, and maintains the concurrency floor.

atoms.statement: Implement fan-out orchestration using the bridge's existing `driver agent-invoke` and `lib/parallel.ps1`, fixing known instabilities (e.g., parallel-pipe, untracked-cleanup, codex hang). The audit fan-out should use a read-only subprocess harness, not `lib/parallel.ps1`'s worktree/merge functions, and be tested with wide-fanout dummy jobs.
atoms.test: Run a wide-fanout stress test (20-30 dummy CLI jobs) using the new read-only harness within `lib/parallel.ps1`, verifying stability, correct stdout/stderr capture, timeout handling, and absence of hangs.

atoms.statement: Implement strict per-agent isolation so that the failure (timeout, crash, empty reply) of a single finder/verifier agent does not abort the entire phase; job status, stderr/artifacts are preserved, and the orchestrator decides on retry or degraded quorum.
atoms.test: Introduce controlled failures (e.g., timeout, crash, malformed output) in individual agents during a multi-agent run and verify that the overall audit continues, failures are logged, and artifacts are preserved.

atoms.statement: Implement comprehensive cost control via a budget profile, enforcing total-agent-caps, token budgets, configurable depth (dimensions, verifiers-per-finding, finder rounds), and including an early-exit for VERIFY if FIND returns zero findings, potentially with a pre-flight cost estimate.
atoms.test: Configure a budget profile with agent caps, token limits, and depth settings; verify that the audit respects these limits, and that an early-exit occurs if FIND yields no findings.

atoms.statement: Create a PROJECT_MAP+PLAN document covering all required aspects (entrypoints, deep-audit/deep-LLM layer, driver agent-invoke, lib/parallel.ps1, backlog writer, scheduler hooks) before any implementation begins.
atoms.test: Verify that a comprehensive PROJECT_MAP+PLAN document is produced and approved by stakeholders before any code implementation starts.

atoms.statement: The FIND phase must accept a configurable list of dimensions and launch all finder jobs for these dimensions simultaneously.
atoms.test: Configure the FIND phase with a custom list of dimensions and verify that agents are spawned for each dimension and run in parallel.

atoms.statement: Each finder agent must return only structured JSON findings conforming to a predefined schema (e.g., root_cause, file, line, evidence_snippet, severity, why, fix_sketch, confidence).
atoms.test: Run a finder agent and validate its output against the specified JSON schema; verify that malformed output is handled (e.g., rejected or repaired).

atoms.statement: The VERIFY phase must be adversarial, treating each finding as false by default. It should spawn all skeptic agents for all findings simultaneously. Each skeptic must cite current file:line evidence to refute a finding; findings are discarded if a majority of skeptics refute them. Refuted findings should be kept in the report.
atoms.test: Provide a set of findings (some true, some false) to the VERIFY phase and verify that skeptics are spawned, findings are correctly refuted/confirmed based on majority rule and evidence citation, and refuted findings are present in the report.

atoms.statement: The SYNTHESIZE phase must deduplicate confirmed findings, rank them by severity, and auto-create actionable, structured backlog fix-tasks (e.g., for critical/high severity) with an idempotency key to prevent duplicates across runs.
atoms.test: Run the SYNTHESIZE phase with confirmed findings, verify that tasks are created in the backlog with correct metadata, severity ranking, and that re-running with the same findings does not create duplicate tasks due to idempotency.

atoms.statement: Finder/verifier agents must use thin prompts and fat tools, passing each agent its dimension and location, and letting the Claude/Codex CLI read the code itself (e.g., `codex -s read-only`, `claude -p --allowedTools Read,Grep,Glob --add-dir`) instead of pre-stuffing large context into stdin.
atoms.test: Verify that agent prompts are concise and that agents are invoked with CLI arguments/flags that enable them to read code directly from the filesystem, rather than receiving large code snippets via stdin.
